base_method_card.title: Forecasting directional movements of stock prices for intraday trading using LSTM and random forests
base_method_card.task_type: cross-sectional binary directional movement forecasting for intraday trading
base_method_card.frequency: daily trading days with intraday return target
base_method_card.horizon: same trading day intraday return direction relative to cross-sectional median
base_method_card.label_definition: For each stock at time t, Class 0 if its intraday return is smaller than the cross-sectional median intraday return of all stocks at time t; Class 1 if its intraday return is bigger than the cross-sectional median intraday return of all stocks at time t.
data_requirements: Daily data for constituent stocks of the S&P 500 from January 1993 through December 2018.
Opening prices and closing prices sufficient to compute returns with respect to closing prices, returns with respect to opening prices, and intraday returns.
For each study window, construct per-stock feature matrices, remove the first 240 partially filled rows, and concatenate training data across all stocks in S.
At each trading day, compute cross-sectional median intraday return across all stocks to form binary labels.
base_method_card.training_protocol: Within a typical study window with Tstudy = 1008 rows, remove the first 240 rows because lagged returns are partially undefined; split remaining rows chronologically with approximately t = 241 to t = 756 for training and t = 757 to t = Tstudy for testing/trading. Concatenate training data for all stocks in S, yielding approximately 500 x 516 = 258000 training instances and 500 x 252 = 126000 trading instances. LSTM uses CuDNNLSTM. Optimizer, loss, batch size, number of epochs, random seed, validation protocol, and early stopping are unknown from the supplied context.
base_method_card.evaluation_protocol: Evaluate the 3-Feature IntraDay LSTM row on the trading/test portion. The trading strategy buys the 10 stocks with the highest predicted probability and sells short the 10 stocks with the lowest predicted probability each trading day, with equal monetary weight, and reports daily returns before transaction costs. The exact outer rolling-window schedule over 1993-2018 is unknown from the supplied context.
base_method_card.cost_assumptions: Returns are reported prior to transaction costs.
strict_requirements: Use the 3-Feature IntraDay LSTM configuration only; do not mix with Random Forest or 1-Feature rows.
Use a 240 trading-day by 3-feature LSTM input representation.
Remove the first 240 rows of each study matrix before splitting.
Use chronological split within each study window: approximately t = 241 to t = 756 for training and t = 757 to t = Tstudy for testing/trading, where typically Tstudy = 1008.
Construct labels using the cross-sectional median intraday return at each time t.
For the trading-strategy evaluation, buy the 10 stocks with the highest probability and short the 10 stocks with the lowest probability, with equal monetary weight.
unknowns: Exact S&P 500 constituent membership construction and survivorship-bias handling.
Exact formulas for all three feature return groups beyond the descriptions supplied.
Exact outer rolling-window schedule over January 1993 to December 2018.
LSTM architecture details other than CuDNNLSTM and input shape, including number of layers, hidden units, dropout, dense layers, activation functions, and initialization.
Optimizer, loss function, learning rate, batch size, number of epochs, early stopping, validation split, random seed, and hardware/GPU details.
Scaling or normalization procedure and whether statistics are fit only on training data.
Transaction cost model, because the reported returns are prior to transaction costs.

base_method_card.preprocessing_protocol: For each stock, construct the feature matrix with M columns and Tstudy rows. For LSTM, M is reported as (240, 3). Remove the top 240 rows because lagged return features are partially undefined for t <= m. Split the remaining rows chronologically into training and testing/trading subsets, then concatenate training data across stocks. Scaling, normalization, missing-data handling beyond row removal, and whether any transform statistics are fit on train data only are unknown from the supplied context.
